props.text:
See everyone first?
Wait for certainty?
…how long should I look before I leap?

beats.narration_text: Four candidates arrive in random order, and every rejection is permanent. If you wait to see all four, you identify the best perfectly—one decision too late. Perfect information gives zero chance to hire.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Four candidates arrive in random order, and every rejection is permanent. If you wait to see all four, you identify the best perfectly, one decision too late. Perfect information gives zero chance to hire.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 1 · Four-card wait-for-all adversary runs; each rejection locks visibly.

beats.narration_text: Now reject only the first candidate as a benchmark, then take the next new record. Across all twenty-four orders, that rule hires the best eleven times. Looking briefly beats looking completely.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Now reject only the first candidate as a benchmark, then take the next new record. Across all twenty four orders, that rule hires the best eleven times. Looking briefly beats looking completely.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 2 · All 24 four-candidate permutations collapse into threshold outcome counts.

beats.narration_text: Try eight candidates ranked from one to eight, where eight is best. We observe the first three: four, seven, then two. Candidate four is a six. Would you stop?
beats.tts_normalized_text: Try eight candidates ranked from one to eight, where eight is best. We observe the first three: four, seven, then two. Candidate four is a six. Would you stop?
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PREDICT · Held commitment over live candidate row; hai-simple text treatment, no static card.

beats.narration_text: Do not stop: six fails to beat the benchmark seven. Candidate five is eight, a new record, so we leap and win. The observation window was not wasted; it manufactured the threshold.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Do not stop: six fails to beat the benchmark seven. Candidate five is eight, a new record, so we leap and win. The observation window was not wasted; it manufactured the threshold.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRANSFORM / TRACE · Same cards advance; explicit OBSERVE, REJECT, ACCEPT states and benchmark table update.

beats.narration_text: Run the same rule on five, seven, two, six, eight, four, three, one. We reject six, accept eight, and win again. But if eight hid inside the first three, the benchmark would become unbeatable and we would lose.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Run the same rule on five, seven, two, six, eight, four, three, one. We reject six, accept eight, and win again. But if eight hid inside the first three, the benchmark would become unbeatable and we would lose.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 3 · Second full trace morphs into its failure permutation without erasing the observation layer.

beats.narration_text: Now the license is visible. The order must be random, the total count known, choices irrevocable, ranks comparable, and the goal the single best. Under look-then-leap, we win exactly when the best arrives after the window and the best earlier rival lies inside it.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Now the license is visible. The order must be random, the total count known, choices irrevocable, ranks comparable, and the goal the single best. Under look then leap, we win exactly when the best arrives after the window and the best earlier rival lies inside it.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE ABSTRACTION · Licensing characteristics named after three instances; invariant shown as two explicit conditions.

beats.narration_text: Sweep the observation window. With four candidates, rejecting one wins eleven of twenty-four orders, the peak. As the crowd grows, the peak slides toward thirty-seven percent observed and thirty-seven percent success—not because thirty-seven is magic, but because information and opportunity balance there.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Sweep the observation window. With four candidates, rejecting one wins eleven of twenty four orders, the peak. As the crowd grows, the peak slides toward thirty seven percent observed and thirty seven percent success, not because thirty seven is magic, but because information and opportunity balance there.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PAYOFF · Hook returns as finite outcome bars transforming into a labeled asymptotic threshold curve; no symbolic equation lands.

beats.narration_text: The verdict: more information is not always more useful. Observe too little and the benchmark is weak; observe too long and the best may already be gone. Look, then leap.
